The problem asks for the second largest integer $m < 200$ such that $3 \nmid m$ and the number of cycles in the permutation $x \mapsto 3x \pmod m$ on the set $\{1, 2, \dots, m-1\}$ is odd.

Let $K(m)$ be the number of cycles. We have shown that $K(m) = \sum_{n|m, n > 1} \frac{\phi(n)}{\text{ord}_n(3)}$, where $\text{ord}_n(3)$ is the smallest integer $k \ge 1$ such that $3^k \equiv 1 \pmod n$.
We iterate through all $m < 200$ such that $3 \nmid m$, calculate $K(m)$, and check if it's odd.

The values of $m < 200$ with $3 \nmid m$ and $K(m)$ being odd are:
2, 5, 7, 10, 14, 17, 19, 22, 26, 29, 31, 34, 38, 41, 43, 46, 50, 53, 55, 58, 62, 65, 67, 70, 74, 77, 79, 82, 86, 89, 91, 94, 98, 101, 103, 106, 110, 113, 115, 118, 122, 125, 127, 130, 134, 137, 139, 142, 146, 149, 151, 154, 158, 161, 163, 166, 170, 173, 175, 178, 182, 185, 187, 190, 194, 197, 199.

The largest such $m$ is 199, and the second largest is 197.

The calculations:
For $m = 199$, 199 is prime and $3 \nmid 199$. $K(199) = N(199) = \phi(199) / \text{ord}_{199}(3)$.
$\phi(199) = 198$.
$\text{ord}_{199}(3)$: $3^k \equiv 1 \pmod{199}$.
$3^1 = 3, 3^2 = 9, 3^3 = 27, 3^4 = 81, 3^5 = 243 \equiv 44, 3^6 = 132, 3^7 = 396 \equiv 197 \equiv -2, 3^{14} \equiv 4, 3^{28} \equiv 16, 3^{56} \equiv 256 \equiv 57, 3^{98} \equiv 3^{56} \cdot 3^{28} \cdot 3^{14} \equiv 57 \cdot 16 \cdot 4 = 3648$.
$3648 = 18 \cdot 199 + 76$. So $3^{98} \equiv 76 \pmod{199}$.
Actually, we just need $K(199)$ to be odd.
$N(199) = 198 / \text{ord}_{199}(3)$. For this to be odd, $\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ must be a multiple of 2, specifically such that the power of 2 in $\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ is the same as in 198.
$198 = 2 \cdot 99$. So $\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ must be of the form $2 \cdot \text{odd}$.
$\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ must divide $\phi(199) = 198$.
Divisors of 198 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 11, 18, 22, 33, 66, 99, 198.
For $N(199) = 198 / \text{ord}_{199}(3)$ to be odd, $\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ must be 2, 6, 18, 22, 66, or 198.
$3^2 = 9 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{199}$.
$3^6 = 729 = 3 \cdot 199 + 132 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{199}$.
$3^{18} = (3^6)^3 \equiv 132^3 \equiv (-67)^3 = -300763$.
$300763 / 199 = 1511.37$.
$3^{18} \pmod{199} \equiv -300763 + 1511 \cdot 199 = -300763 + 300689 = -74 \equiv 125$.
$3^{22} = 3^{18} \cdot 3^4 \equiv 125 \cdot 81 = 10125$.
$10125 / 199 \approx 50.87$. $10125 - 50 \cdot 199 = 10125 - 9950 = 175 \equiv -24$.
$3^{66} = (3^{22})^3 \equiv (-24)^3 = -13824$.
$13824 / 199 \approx 69.46$. $-13824 + 70 \cdot 199 = -13824 + 13930 = 106$.
$3^{99} = 3^{98} \cdot 3 \equiv 76 \cdot 3 = 228 \equiv 29 \pmod{199}$.
Since $3^{99} \equiv 29 \not\equiv 1$, $\text{ord}_{199}(3)$ is not a divisor of 99, so it must be 198 (since it's a divisor of 198 and $3^{99} \neq 1$).
$N(199) = 198 / 198 = 1$, which is odd.
For $m = 197$, 197 is prime. $K(197) = N(197) = 196 / \text{ord}_{197}(3)$.
For $N(197)$ to be odd, $\text{ord}_{197}(3)$ must contain all the powers of 2 in 196.
$196 = 4 \cdot 49$. So $\text{ord}_{197}(3)$ must be a multiple of 4.
$3^4 = 81 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{197}$.
$\text{ord}_{197}(3)$ divides $\phi(197) = 196$. Divisors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28, 49, 98, 196.
$3^1=3, 3^2=9, 3^4=81, 3^7=2187 = 11 \cdot 197 + 20 \equiv 20$.
$3^{14} \equiv 20^2 = 400 = 2 \cdot 197 + 6 \equiv 6$.
$3^{28} \equiv 6^2 = 36$.
$3^{49} = 3^{28} \cdot 3^{14} \cdot 3^7 \equiv 36 \cdot 6 \cdot 20 = 4320 = 21 \cdot 197 + 183 \equiv -14$.
$3^{98} \equiv (-14)^2 = 196 \equiv -1 \pmod{197}$.
So $\text{ord}_{197}(3) = 196$.
$N(197) = 196 / 196 = 1$, which is odd.
